symbols.name: n
symbols.def: Number of source-trial observations.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Number of target-population covariate observations.

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: Polynomial source-depletion exponent at the left boundary.

symbols.name: s
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of each source conditional response.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the nonsingular source and target density factors.

symbols.name: \gamma
symbols.def: Nominal noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: Asymptotic target-to-source sample-size ratio.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Common radius for boundedness and Hölder conditions.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: Known treatment-randomization positivity constant.

symbols.name: c_{S,-}
symbols.def: Lower bound for the nonsingular source density factor.

symbols.name: c_{S,+}
symbols.def: Upper bound for the nonsingular source density factor.

symbols.name: c_{T,-}
symbols.def: Lower bound for the target density.

symbols.name: c_{T,+}
symbols.def: Upper bound for the target density.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: One-dimensional baseline covariate support with a distinguished left boundary.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Baseline covariate in the population specified by context.

symbols.name: A
symbols.def: Randomized treatment in the source trial.

symbols.name: Y^S(d)
symbols.def: Source-trial potential outcome under treatment \(d\).

symbols.name: Y^T(d)
symbols.def: Target-population potential outcome under treatment \(d\).

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: Observed source outcome, equal to \(Y^S(A)\) under consistency.

symbols.name: O^S
symbols.def: Source observation \(O^S=(X,A,Y)\).

symbols.name: W^S
symbols.def: Full-data source unit \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\).

symbols.name: X^T
symbols.def: Target-population covariate observation.

symbols.name: W^T
symbols.def: Full-data target unit \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\).

symbols.name: F^S_{n,m}
symbols.def: Source full-data law at triangular-array index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: F^T_{n,m}
symbols.def: Target full-data law at triangular-array index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: \pi_S
symbols.def: Source observed-data projection \(\pi_S(x,d,y_0,y_1)=(x,d,y_d)\).

symbols.name: \pi_T
symbols.def: Target observed-data projection \(\pi_T(x,y_0,y_1)=x\).

symbols.name: \mathcal D_{n,m}
symbols.def: Observed data \(\mathcal D_{n,m}=((O_i^S)_{i=1}^n,(X_j^T)_{j=1}^m)\).

symbols.name: P_S
symbols.def: Observed source-trial law \(P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m}\) at index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: P_T
symbols.def: Observed target law \(P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m}\) at index \((n,m)\).

symbols.name: \mathbb P_{n,m}
symbols.def: Triangular-array observed-data law \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) of \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

symbols.name: f_S
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of the \(X\)-marginal of \(P_S\).

symbols.name: f_T
symbols.def: Lebesgue density of \(P_T\).

symbols.name: g_S
symbols.def: Nonsingular source factor \(g_S(x)=x^{-a}f_S(x)\) for \(x>0\), extended continuously to \(x=0\).

symbols.name: g_T
symbols.def: Nonsingular target factor \(g_T(x)=f_T(x)\).

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: Known trial randomization probability \(e(x)=P_S(A=1\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: \mu_0
symbols.def: Source control response \(\mu_0(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=0,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu_1
symbols.def: Source treated response \(\mu_1(x)=\mathbb E_{P_S}[Y\mid A=1,X=x]\).

symbols.name: \mu
symbols.def: Transportable conditional effect \(\mu(x)=\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: Identified observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]\); under the identification assumptions it equals the target average treatment effect.

symbols.name: r
symbols.def: Transport Riesz weight \(r(x)=f_T(x)/f_S(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: Randomized-trial contrast \(Z=AY/e(X)-(1-A)Y/\{1-e(X)\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H^u(M)
symbols.def: The radius \(M\) Hölder ball of order \(u>0\) on \(\mathcal X\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: Local-polynomial order \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\).

symbols.name: C_{\mathrm{LP}}
symbols.def: Operator-norm constant for the order \(p\) boundary local-polynomial remainder on the unit Hölder ball.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: A fixed nonzero \(C^\infty\) bump supported on \([0,1]\) with Hölder norm at most one.

symbols.name: \rho_n(a,s)
symbols.def: Source root-risk rate \(\rho_n(a,s)=n^{-1/2}\) for \(a<1\), \(\rho_n(a,s)=\sqrt{\log n/n}\) for \(a=1\), and \(\rho_n(a,s)=n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) for \(a>1\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: Spline degree \(q=\lceil\max\{s,t\}\rceil\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B_{h,J}
symbols.def: Degree \(q\) normalized B-spline space with \(J\) endpoint-repeated equally spaced knot intervals and dimension \(J+q\), including the constant function.

symbols.name: c_{\mathrm{OT}}
symbols.def: Squared Euclidean transport cost \(c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)=|x-z|^2\).

symbols.name: \eta_0
symbols.def: Fixed entropic regularization level.

symbols.name: \lambda_0
symbols.def: Fixed source-marginal relaxation level.

symbols.name: \xi_n
symbols.def: Calibration-slack penalty \(\xi_n=n^2\).

symbols.name: K_0
symbols.def: Fixed number of cross-fitting folds, \(K_0=5\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Index of a deterministic source or target validation fold.

symbols.name: i
symbols.def: Index of a source observation.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: Index of a target observation.

symbols.name: \mathcal T^S_k
symbols.def: Source training complement \(\mathcal T^S_k=\{i:1+((i-1)\bmod K_0)\ne k\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal T^T_k
symbols.def: Target training complement \(\mathcal T^T_k=\{j:1+((j-1)\bmod K_0)\ne k\}\).

symbols.name: k_S
symbols.def: Deterministic assignment \(k_S(i)=1+((i-1)\bmod K_0)\).

symbols.name: k_T
symbols.def: Deterministic assignment \(k_T(j)=1+((j-1)\bmod K_0)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V^S_k
symbols.def: Source validation fold \(\mathcal V^S_k=\{i:k_S(i)=k\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal V^T_k
symbols.def: Target validation fold \(\mathcal V^T_k=\{j:k_T(j)=k\}\).

symbols.name: N^S_k
symbols.def: Source validation-fold size \(N^S_k=|\mathcal V^S_k|\).

symbols.name: N^T_k
symbols.def: Target validation-fold size \(N^T_k=|\mathcal V^T_k|\).

symbols.name: \mathbf R_h
symbols.def: Scaled boundary basis \(\mathbf R_h(x)=(1,x/h,\ldots,(x/h)^p)^\top\).

symbols.name: \widehat G_{k,h}
symbols.def: Fold-trained ridge Gram matrix defined in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\alpha_{k,h}
symbols.def: Unique fold-trained boundary ridge coefficient defined in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: The class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:model\text{-}class}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)
symbols.def: Worst-case root-mean-squared risk constructed in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\text{-}risk}\).

symbols.name: b_h
symbols.def: Least-favorable boundary bump constructed from \(K\) at scale \(h\).

symbols.name: \mathbf b_{h,J}
symbols.def: Canonical left-to-right standard normalized degree-\(q\) B-spline basis \(\mathbf b_{h,J}=(N_1,\ldots,N_{J+q})^\top\) of \(\mathcal B_{h,J}\); the basis forms a partition of unity, but no individual coordinate is designated as the constant function.

symbols.name: \widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}
symbols.def: The vector \((N_2,\ldots,N_{J+q})^\top\) obtained from the standard normalized basis \(\mathbf b_{h,J}=(N_1,\ldots,N_{J+q})^\top\); together with the separate constant coordinate it spans \(\mathcal B_{h,J}\).

symbols.name: \widehat P^S_h
symbols.def: For fold \(k\), the training-complement interior source measure \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h=|\mathcal T^S_k|^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\delta_{X_i}\); the fold superscript is suppressed when context fixes \(k\).

symbols.name: \widehat P^T_h
symbols.def: For fold \(k\), the training-complement interior target measure \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h=|\mathcal T^T_k|^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\delta_{X_j^T}\); the fold superscript is suppressed when context fixes \(k\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Pi_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass branch, the unique exact-feasibility or penalized semi-unbalanced entropic optimizer constructed in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\); on the zero-interior-mass branch, the zero finite measure is a deterministic fallback and is not asserted to couple a nonzero target marginal.

symbols.name: \widehat\theta_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass exact-feasibility branch, the selected multiplier for the \(J+q-1\) explicit nonconstant spline-calibration equations; on a positive-interior-mass penalized branch, the corresponding quadratic-penalty gradient multiplier; on the zero-interior-mass branch, the deterministic zero vector.

symbols.name: \widehat\psi_{h,J}
symbols.space: real vectors indexed by interior target training observations
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass optimization branch, the selected target-marginal KKT multiplier, jointly minimum-norm with the calibration multiplier where applicable; on the zero-interior-mass branch, the deterministic zero vector.

symbols.name: J_{\mu,n}
symbols.def: Deterministic interior regression knot-interval count \(J_{\mu,n}=\lceil n^{1/(2s+1)}\rceil\); the associated degree-\(q\) standard spline basis has \(J_{\mu,n}+q\) coefficients.

symbols.name: J_{r,n}
symbols.def: Deterministic interior calibration knot-interval count \(J_{r,n}=\lceil(n/\log n)^{1/(2t+1)}\rceil\) for \(n\ge2\), with \(J_{r,1}=1\); the associated degree-\(q\) standard spline space has dimension \(J_{r,n}+q\).

symbols.name: \widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Unique fold-trained ridge coefficient for the full \(J_{\mu,n}+q\)-coordinate standard spline basis in \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\).

symbols.name: \widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Untruncated order-\(p\) boundary local-polynomial fit spliced to an interior degree-\(q\) regression spline with \(J_{\mu,n}\) knot intervals and \(J_{\mu,n}+q\) coefficients.

symbols.name: \widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: On a positive-interior-mass optimization branch, the exponential continuation of the selected primal--dual solution that agrees with the first-marginal density at source training atoms; on the zero-interior-mass branch it is the identically zero deterministic fallback.

symbols.name: \widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT}}_{h,J}
symbols.def: The pointwise projection of \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}\) onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\), with the identically zero deterministic fallback on a zero-interior-mass branch. It is measurable and bounded, but it need not inherit the raw plan's training-atom spline-calibration equations.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Boundary-spliced Riesz-calibrated transport estimator indexed by separate regression and calibration knot-interval counts \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\). Its full regression coefficient dimension is \(J_{\mu,n}+q\), its full calibration spline-space dimension is \(J_{r,n}+q\), and its explicit nonconstant calibration vector has dimension \(J_{r,n}+q-1\) because the target-marginal mass equation supplies the constant coordinate.

symbols.name: \widehat H_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Observable fold-trained interior ridge Gram matrix for the full \(J_{\mu,n}+q\)-coordinate standard spline basis in the linear-coefficient construction.

symbols.name: L_{i,k,h,J_{\mu,n}}
symbols.def: Coefficient of source pseudo-outcome \(Z_i\) in the fold-\(k\) boundary-spliced regression evaluation.

symbols.name: \Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
symbols.def: Coefficient of \(Z_i\) in the exact covariate-conditional linear expansion of the unchanged spliced estimator.

symbols.name: B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
symbols.def: Worst-case realized source--target design discrepancy over the bounded radius-\(2M\) Hölder class.

symbols.name: R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
symbols.def: Bounded-outcome Hoeffding radius for the source pseudo-outcome linear term.

symbols.name: R_T(m)
symbols.def: Bounded-outcome Hoeffding radius \(\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}\) for the target empirical mean.

symbols.name: \beta
symbols.def: Fractional Hölder exponent \(\beta=s-p\), where \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\).

symbols.name: G_h^{\circ}(P)
symbols.def: Oracle boundary Gram matrix constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: q_h^{\circ}(P)
symbols.def: Oracle target boundary moment constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)
symbols.def: Law-indexed boundary local-polynomial weight constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: \omega_h^{\circ}(x;P)
symbols.def: Law-indexed boundary-corrected oracle weight constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak b_h(v;P)
symbols.def: Signed law-indexed boundary approximation bias constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: b_h^{\circ}(P)
symbols.def: Worst-case fixed-Hölder boundary allowance constructed in \(\mathrm{def:oracle\text{-}boundary\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}weight}\).

symbols.name: \overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
symbols.def: Certified finite jet-linear-program upper radius constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}
symbols.def: Finite-sample Hoeffding execution-certificate interval constructed in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\) with executable certified bias radius \(\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\).

assumptions.condition: \(e\) is fixed and known by the source-trial randomization protocol.
\(\mathbb E_{F^T_{n,m}}[Y^T(d)\mid X^T=x]=\mathbb E_{F^S_{n,m}}[Y^S(d)\mid X=x]=\mu_d(x)\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_T\)-almost every \(x\).

novel.justification: The condition permits polynomial depletion of trial enrollment at a clinically meaningful covariate boundary. Beta-type enrollment densities and smooth exponential tilts of \(x^a\) satisfy it, so it describes a concrete weak-overlap mechanism rather than an estimator-dependent rate restriction.

standard.name: target density bounded away from zero and infinity

assumptions.condition: \(\operatorname{Var}(Y\mid A=d,X=x)\ge M^{-1}\) for every \(d\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_S\)-almost every \(x\).

definitions.name: Polynomial-boundary transport class
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\bigl\{\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}:\exists(F^S_{n,m},F^T_{n,m})\text{ with }P_S=(\pi_S)_\#F^S_{n,m},\ P_T=(\pi_T)_\#F^T_{n,m},\text{ and every listed member-property assumption holds at the fixed indices }(n,m,a,s,t)\bigr\}.\] The finite-\((n,m)\) class contains no condition on how \(m/n\) behaves along a sequence.

definitions.name: Two-sample minimax root risk
definitions.construction: \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)=\inf_{\widehat\tau}\sup_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\Bigl\{\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}[(\widehat\tau-\tau)^2]\Bigr\}^{1/2},\] where the infimum ranges over all estimators measurable with respect to \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\).

definitions.name: Executable cross-fitted boundary regression
definitions.construction:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
For the interior spline, \(J_{\mu,n}\) is the number of knot intervals and
\[
d_{\mu,n}=J_{\mu,n}+q.
\]
Let
\[
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)
=\bigl(N_{1,h,J_{\mu,n}}(x),\ldots,N_{d_{\mu,n},h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)\bigr)^\top
\in\mathbb R^{d_{\mu,n}}
\]
be the full standard normalized degree-\(q\) B-spline basis for the endpoint-repeated equally spaced knots. Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{d_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}
\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered standard bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.

definitions.name: Executable interior RiCOT weights and certificate role
definitions.construction:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Put
\[
d_{r,n}=J_{r,n}+q,
\qquad
\mathbf b_{h,J_{r,n}}=(N_1,\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}})^\top,
\]
where \((N_1,\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}})\) is the standard left-to-right normalized degree-\(q\) B-spline basis for the \(J_{r,n}\) endpoint-repeated equally spaced knot intervals on \([h,1]\). Define the equivalent calibration coordinates
\[
\boldsymbol\phi_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\bigl(1,N_2(x),\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}}(x)\bigr)^\top,
\qquad
\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\bigl(N_2(x),\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}}(x)\bigr)^\top
\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}.
\]
The partition-of-unity identity gives
\[
N_1(x)=1-\sum_{\ell=2}^{d_{r,n}}N_\ell(x),
\]
so \(\boldsymbol\phi_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\mathbf b_{h,J_{r,n}}\) span the same spline space.

If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set the calibration vector in \(\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}\) and every target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)
=\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
Because \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) implies
\[
\Pi_1([h,1])=\Pi_2([h,1])=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h([h,1]),
\]
the separate target-mass constraint supplies the constant coordinate. Together with the preceding \(d_{r,n}-1\) equations and the identity for \(N_1\), it is equivalent to calibration of the full space \(\mathcal B_{h,J_{r,n}}\).

If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi
+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)
+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)
-\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)
\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let
\[
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}
\]
and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}
\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1},
\]
and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}
\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)
+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)
+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}
\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)
=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration knot-interval count.

Both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight are measurable functions of the observed covariates. In the execution certificate the capped downstream weight enters only through the observable coefficients \(\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\). The cap still does not inherit the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations, and no held-out localization, coefficient-norm rate, leverage bound, or frontier attainment is claimed.

definitions.name: Observable RiCOT linear coefficients
Riesz-calibrated boundary-spliced estimator and linear carrier
definitions.construction:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The capped downstream weight is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup; only the raw \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}\) has KKT-continuation and training-atom density status. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The indices \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\) are respectively regression and calibration knot-interval counts, not coefficient dimensions. The full regression coefficient dimension is \(J_{\mu,n}+q\), the full calibration spline-space dimension is \(J_{r,n}+q\), and the explicit nonconstant calibration vector has dimension \(J_{r,n}+q-1\) because the target-marginal mass equation supplies the constant coordinate. Only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.

After the covariates are fixed, the foldwise ridge fits are linear in the source pseudo-outcomes. With the observable coefficients defined in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\), algebraic expansion of the unchanged display gives
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i.
\]
This equality is proved in \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\); it records the estimator's certificate carrier without modifying its folds, fits, weights, or formula.

definitions.name: Finite certified Hölder jet-LP design discrepancy
definitions.construction:
For this certificate use the following H\"older convention. Put \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\) and \(\beta=s-p\in(0,1]\). For \(L>0\),
\[
\mathcal H^s(L)=\left\{v\in C^p([0,1]):
\max_{0\le r\le p}\|v^{(r)}\|_\infty\le L,
\quad
[v^{(p)}]_{\beta}:=\sup_{x\ne y}\frac{|v^{(p)}(x)-v^{(p)}(y)|}{|x-y|^\beta}\le L
\right\}.
\]
For integers \(n,m\ge2\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), let \(z_1<\cdots<z_N\) be the distinct sites among \(X_1,\ldots,X_n,X_1^T,\ldots,X_m^T\), and set
\[
c_\ell=\sum_{i:X_i=z_\ell}\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})-
\frac1m\#\{j:X_j^T=z_\ell\}.
\]
Retain the abstract design discrepancy
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=
\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\ \|v\|_\infty\le1}}
\left|\sum_{\ell=1}^Nc_\ell v(z_\ell)\right|.
\]
For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), let \(V_\sigma\) be the optimal value of the finite linear program
\[
\operatorname{maximize}_{(u_{\ell,r})}\quad
\sigma\sum_{\ell=1}^Nc_\ell u_{\ell,0}
\]
over \(N(p+1)\) real variables \(u_{\ell,r}\), \(1\le\ell\le N\), \(0\le r\le p\), subject to
\[
|u_{\ell,0}|\le1,
\qquad
|u_{\ell,r}|\le2M\quad(1\le r\le p),
\]
and, for every \(1\le\ell,k\le N\) and \(0\le r\le p\),
\[
\left|u_{\ell,r}-\sum_{q=r}^p
u_{k,q}\frac{(z_\ell-z_k)^{q-r}}{(q-r)!}\right|
\le
2M\frac{\Gamma(\beta+1)}{\Gamma(s-r+1)}|z_\ell-z_k|^{s-r}.
\]
Each absolute-value restriction means its two one-sided linear inequalities. Define the certified jet-LP radius
\[
\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=\max\{V_{-1},V_1\}.
\]
The two programs have \(N(p+1)\) variables and \(O\{N^2(p+1)\}\) linear inequalities. Every admissible H\"older trace is feasible, so
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}).
\]
For \(0<s\le1\) the reduction is exact by H\"older--McShane extension. For \(s>1\) it is a certified conservative jet relaxation, not an asserted exact finite Whitney characterization. Both optimal values are finite because of the box constraints. No stochastic-order or frontier-order claim is part of this definition.

definitions.name: Observable coefficient norm and Hoeffding radii
definitions.construction:
For integers \(n,m\ge2\), define the observable source and target Hoeffding radii
\[
R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})
=\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2},
\qquad
R_T(m)=\sqrt{\frac{2\log(4/\gamma)}{m}}.
\]
The only source dispersion diagnostic used by the certificate is the exact observable coefficient norm \(\{\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\}^{1/2}\). No empirical variance estimator, covariance estimator, studentization, leverage condition, Gaussian approximation, or multiplier approximation is part of this construction.

definitions.name: Finite-sample executable RiCOT certificate interval
Oracle boundary local-polynomial linear weight
definitions.construction:
For \(P\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), let \(P_S\) and \(P_T\) denote its source and target component laws and define
\[
G_h^{\circ}(P)=\int_0^h\mathbf R_h(x)\mathbf R_h(x)^\top f_S(x)\,dx,
\qquad
q_h^{\circ}(P)=\int_0^h\mathbf R_h(x)f_T(x)\,dx.
\]
Whenever \(G_h^{\circ}(P)\) is invertible, define
\[
w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)=\mathbf 1\{x<h\}\mathbf R_h(x)^\top
\{G_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{-1}q_h^{\circ}(P),
\qquad
\omega_h^{\circ}(x;P)=w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)+r(x)\mathbf 1\{x\ge h\}.
\]
For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\) with \(\|v\|_\infty\le1\), define the signed boundary approximation bias and its class allowance by
\[
\mathfrak b_h(v;P)=\int_0^h\{w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)f_S(x)-f_T(x)\}v(x)\,dx,
\qquad
b_h^{\circ}(P)=\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\\|v\|_\infty\le1}}|\mathfrak b_h(v;P)|.
\]
These are oracle population objects because they use \(f_S\) and \(f_T\). Their invertibility, polynomial reproduction, norm orders, and bias bounds are properties to be proved, not parts of this construction.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) and \(h\downarrow0\), \[\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2=\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\asymp\begin{cases}1,&a<1,\\ \log(1/h),&a=1,\\ h^{1-a},&a>1.\end{cases}\] Hence the target expectation functional has a source \(L^2(P_S)\) Riesz representer if and only if \(a<1\).
statements.justification: This norm is the precise regularity threshold behind the regular, critical, and nonregular regimes.
statements.gap: The transported control-regression component in Burman et al.'s distinct target-outcome estimand uses a density-ratio representer under bounded overlap, while Khan and Tamer link large inverse weights to irregularity without computing this polynomial-boundary threshold for the present covariate-only target functional.
statements.consumer: The lemma tells analysts of the RICOT cardiomyopathy transport study whether an ordinary influence-function variance is finite before fitting a transport estimator.

statements.statement: Suppose \(t>0\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). There are constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for every sufficiently small \(h\), the perturbations generated by \(b_h\) yield two observed-data laws \(\mathbb P_{+,h},\mathbb P_{-,h}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\) whose source marginals satisfy \[\operatorname{KL}(P_{+,h}^{S,n},P_{-,h}^{S,n})\le Cnh^{2s+a+1},\qquad |\tau(\mathbb P_{+,h})-\tau(\mathbb P_{-,h})|\ge ch^{s+1}.\] A separate smooth target-density perturbation yields two full-data laws whose observed target projections have divergence bounded by a constant and target separation at least \(cm^{-1/2}\).
statements.justification: The witness converts the boundary geometry into the exact testing separation needed for the converse.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. define \(\mathcal V\) by the uniform bound \(\sup_x p^*(x)/p^\circ(x)\le B\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; that construction does not cover a diverging polynomial boundary ratio, produce the exponent \((s+1)/(2s+a+1)\), or include the independent target-sample floor.
statements.consumer: The witness certifies that no alternative weighting method can improve the proposed cardiomyopathy transport rate merely by changing the optimizer.

statements.statement: For fixed \(a,s,t,M,\varepsilon,c_{S,-},c_{S,+},c_{T,-},c_{T,+}\) with \(t>0\), \(M\ge a+1\), and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\), there is \(c>0\) such that \[\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}.\] At \(a=1\), the source term is \(c\sqrt{\log n/n}\); it is obtained by a multiscale mixture of boundary bumps and has no hidden polynomial loss.
statements.justification: The converse is the theorem-level certificate that the three regimes are structural rather than artifacts of truncation.
statements.gap: Khan and Tamer establish tail-dependent irregularity. Zhang et al.'s uniformly bounded-ratio class is defined in Section 1 on page 2 and its known-law lower bound is Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12; neither result derives the two-sample polynomial-boundary phase diagram or its critical logarithm.
statements.consumer: The result gives trial planners a lower bound on how much source recruitment near an underrepresented cardiomyopathy-risk boundary is needed for a desired precision.

statements.statement:
Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), the unchanged spliced estimator and the observable coefficients in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\) satisfy the exact identity
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i
\]
and the exact error decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau
={}&\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\\
&+\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\mu(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)\right\}\\
&+\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The middle term is bounded in absolute value by
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}),
\]
where \(\overline B_X\) is the finite certified jet-LP radius in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\). Consequently,
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau\right|
\le \overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
For any realized covariate design with \(\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), the displayed certificate radius is at most
\[
b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}.
\]
This is a finite-sample execution certificate. It makes no stochastic-order, localization, leverage, minimax-attainment, or expected-length claim for \(B_X\), \(\overline B_X\), or the coefficient norm.
statements.justification: The corrected claim converts the unchanged executable estimator into an exact covariate-conditional linear representation and an observable finite-sample certificate based on the jet-LP radius.
statements.gap: Held-out capped-weight localization and coefficient-norm rates are not established, so the result exposes \(\overline B_X\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i^2\) rather than assuming their frontier order.
statements.consumer: A RiCOT cardiomyopathy analysis can compute every radius component and audit whether the realized source--target design supports a useful certificate.

statements.statement:
For arbitrary fixed \(s>0\) and \(t>0\), in the special case \(a=0\),
\[
\frac{c_{T,-}}{c_{S,+}}\le r(x)=\frac{g_T(x)}{g_S(x)}\le\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}},\qquad 0<x\le1,
\]
\(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and
\[
h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).
\]
For every fold whose source and target interior training measures are both nonzero, the capped downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(x)\) is strictly positive for every \(x\in[h_n,1]\). These deterministic facts do not by themselves assert an empirical norm bound, a nonzero realized residual sum, or a root-risk bound.
statements.justification: The bounded-ratio arithmetic is proved for arbitrary fixed \(t>0\), while empirical norm, residual, and root-risk conclusions correctly remain outside this deterministic proposition.
statements.gap: Positive capped downstream weight on a realized nonzero-interior branch is not a variance, localization, or risk bound.
statements.consumer: The \(a=0\) case is a future implementation unit test for positive held-out corrections and the regular oracle scaling, not evidence of empirical frontier attainment.

statements.statement:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(M\ge a+1\) and \(t>0\), along every sequence with \(m/n\to\kappa\), there is \(c>0\) such that
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\left\{m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}
n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\
\sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\
n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.
\end{cases}\right\}.
\]
This lower phase diagram requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds. Moreover, writing \(P=(P_S,P_T)\) for the pair of one-observation laws associated with \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\), uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
|\mathfrak b_{h_n}(\mu;P)|\le b_{h_n}^{\circ}(P)\le C h_n^{s+1}
\]
and
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}
+n^{-1/2}\|\omega_{h_n}^{\circ}(\cdot;P)\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
For every fixed \(a>0\), the deterministic allowance is class-sharp, although the actual bias may vanish for special laws. Thus the proved minimax lower frontier matches the boundary-corrected oracle allowance and linear-weight benchmark. The benchmark is a population oracle calculation; no data-measurable minimax upper bound or frontier-attainment conclusion is asserted.
statements.justification: The theorem states the maximal proved one-sided minimax lower phase diagram and pairs it with the boundary-corrected oracle allowance and linear-weight benchmark, without per-law exactness, measurable attainment, or a minimax-upper implication.
statements.gap: No measurable data-driven estimator is proved to attain the oracle envelope because empirical capped-RiCOT localization and coefficient control remain unresolved.
statements.consumer: The result supplies a precision impossibility and a population oracle benchmark for transported effects under polynomial boundary depletion.

statements.statement:
Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). The interval \(\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\) satisfies the finite-sample fixed-class coverage guarantee
\[
\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}
\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
Its realized length is exactly
\[
2\{\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\}.
\]
In particular, on any realized covariate design for which \(\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), its length is at most
\[
2\left\{b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}\right\}.
\]
The bias radius is computable as the two finite linear programs in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}envelope}\), each with \(N(p+1)\) variables and \(O\{N^2(p+1)\}\) inequalities, where \(N\) is the number of distinct observed covariate sites defined there. No expected-length rate, Gaussian approximation, multiplier approximation, variance consistency, leverage control, or empirical frontier attainment is asserted.
statements.justification: The corrected symmetric interval obtains fixed-class finite-sample coverage from a finite Hölder jet-LP envelope and bounded-sum concentration.
statements.gap: Coverage requires no studentization or Gaussian approximation, but no theorem controls expected length at the minimax frontier.
statements.consumer: The application can report this interval as a fixed-class realized-design guarantee while separately disclosing the absence of a frontier-order length theorem.

statements.statement: Fix \(a>1\), \(t>0\), and \(0<s_1<s_2\), and suppose \(M\ge a+1\) and \(c_{T,-}<1<c_{T,+}\). Any confidence interval with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\gamma\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_1,t)\cup\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\) has, at some law in \(\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s_2,t)\), expected length at least \(c\{m^{-1/2}+n^{-(s_1+1)/(2s_1+a+1)}\}\).
statements.justification: The theorem prevents data-driven smoothness selection from being advertised as honest without an explicit restriction that makes boundary bias observable.
statements.gap: Cai and Low characterize adaptation by between-class moduli, but the ordered modulus for a transported functional under source density \(x^a\), including the transition through \(a=1\), has not been computed.
statements.consumer: The result tells clinical transport analysts when prespecifying a smoothness class is unavoidable for valid interval length claims.

sampling_model.design: At each triangular-array index \((n,m)\), the observed law is \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), induced by full-data laws \(F^S_{n,m}\) and \(F^T_{n,m}\) through the projections \(\pi_S\) and \(\pi_T\). The condition \(m/n\to\kappa\) applies only to theorem sequences.
sampling_model.units: Source full-data units are \(W^S=(X,A,Y^S(0),Y^S(1))\) and are observed as \(O^S=\pi_S(W^S)=(X,A,Y)\); target full-data units are \(W^T=(X^T,Y^T(0),Y^T(1))\) and are observed only as \(X^T=\pi_T(W^T)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary source treatment has known probability \(e(X)\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The source density is \(f_S(x)=x^ag_S(x)\), where \(c_{S,-}\le g_S\le c_{S,+}\) and \(0<c_{S,-}\le a+1\le c_{S,+}\); the target density is \(f_T(x)=g_T(x)\), where \(c_{T,-}\le g_T\le c_{T,+}\) and \(0<c_{T,-}\le1\le c_{T,+}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Under the separate primitive conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, deterministic five-fold regression uses ridge-regularized order-\(p\) boundary local polynomials and degree-\(q\) interior B-splines. Interior weights solve the squared-distance semi-unbalanced entropic program with schedules \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), equally spaced knots, and \(J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\); normalized dual potentials give a measurable exponential extension evaluated on held-out source covariates. Inference uses the displayed fold-centered source and target multiplier process and the displayed target, interior-source, boundary-source, and source-covariance variance terms.

estimand_functional: \(\tau=\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu(X)]=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\), targeted by the unchanged \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) using the capped downstream RiCOT weight. Here \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\) count regression and calibration knot intervals, giving \(J_{\mu,n}+q\) regression coefficients and a \(J_{r,n}+q\)-dimensional calibration spline space with \(J_{r,n}+q-1\) explicit nonconstant equations. Conditional on the covariates, the estimator has the exact observable expansion \(\sum_i\Gamma_i Z_i\). The finite-sample interval uses the computable certified jet-linear-program radius \(\overline B_X\), with \(B_X\le\overline B_X\), together with \(R_S+R_T\). The proved rate result is a one-sided minimax lower phase diagram paired with a boundary-corrected oracle local-polynomial linear-weight benchmark based on \(G_h^{\circ}(P)\), \(q_h^{\circ}(P)\), \(w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)\), and \(\omega_h^{\circ}(x;P)\). Its actual boundary bias \(|\mathfrak b_{h_n}(\mu;P)|\) is at most \(C h_n^{s+1}\), while the explicit allowance \(h_n^{s+1}\) and oracle standard deviation have frontier order; the allowance is class-sharp for fixed \(a>0\), but the actual bias may vanish for special laws. This oracle benchmark is not a data-measurable minimax upper bound; held-out capped-weight localization, empirical frontier attainment, frontier-order expected length, and executable adaptation remain open.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their target-outcome estimand and bounded-overlap RiCOT theory inform the unchanged transport kernel, but do not provide polynomial-boundary held-out localization for the capped continuation used here.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The present note preserves their optimization motivation and proves only an observable finite-sample execution certificate for its distinct covariate-only target functional.

tldr: A randomized trial may contain progressively fewer patients near a clinically important covariate boundary even when the real-world target population retains positive mass there. In the full-data triangular-array model, the causal target is identified as the observed-law integral \(\tau=\int_0^1\{\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)\}f_T(x)\,dx\). The source contribution to root mean-squared error is \(n^{-1/2}\) below the square-integrability threshold \(a=1\), becomes \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) at the threshold, and is \(n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)}\) above it, in addition to the independent target-sample term \(m^{-1/2}\). Under the separate conditions \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, a fully specified squared-distance Riesz-calibrated semi-unbalanced transport program is truncated to the overlap interior and spliced to a deterministic boundary local polynomial. Matching bump and multiscale lower bounds, a fully evaluable fixed-Hölder-class interval with a \(2M\) bias envelope and explicit foldwise multiplier and covariance terms, and a nonadaptation theorem complete the fixed-class program; honest joint adaptation is posed only on an explicit boundary self-similar subclass.

project_justification.gap: Regular Riesz-calibrated transport theory assumes enough overlap for a square-integrable representer, whereas irregular inverse-weight theory does not compute the sharp two-sample Hölder boundary frontier or its critical logarithm.
project_justification.niche: Polynomial trial depletion with a positive target boundary density creates an estimable causal mean whose information geometry changes exactly at \(a=1\); the target sample also imposes a separate parametric floor.
project_justification.fill: Under the separate primitive requirements \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, the project derives the matching modulus, derives optimizer stability for an executable calibrated-transport plus local-polynomial estimator, and provides fixed-class honest intervals with a fold-centered joint calibration--boundary multiplier envelope and an explicit covariance-complete standard error while making the self-similarity requirement for adaptation explicit.

related_work: Burman et al. (2026) are the optimization and application anchor, not a nested estimand comparator. Their target unit contains an observed outcome. Proposition 2.1 on page 6 identifies \(\tau_Q=\mathbb E_Q[Y^Q]-\mathbb E_Q[\mu_0(X^Q)]\), while Theorem 3.1 on pages 6--7 gives its efficient influence function; this core instead observes only target covariates and targets \(\mathbb E_{P_T}[\mu_1(X)-\mu_0(X)]\). Their Assumption 1(iv) on page 7 imposes bounded target-to-trial density ratio, Theorem 4.5 on pages 13--14 proves calibrated-weight consistency, Theorem 5.2 on page 16 gives efficient inference for their estimand, and Section 8 on pages 23--24 studies 30-month mortality in transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Section S4.3 is the source locator for the standard one-dimensional density-ratio calibration-sieve threshold \(t>1/2\). That threshold is separate from \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), which controls the distinct nuisance-product remainder. The present transport program is informed by their semi-unbalanced entropic geometry without claiming that its \(a=0\) case reproduces their theorem. Khan and Tamer (2010) establish the general connection between arbitrarily large inverse weights and slower-than-parametric estimation, but do not analyze a two-sample transported Hölder functional. Zhang et al. (2025) define the uniformly bounded likelihood-ratio class \(\mathcal V\) in Section 1 on page 2 and state its minimax lower bound as Theorem 1 in Appendix A.1 on page 12. Their observation model and Sobolev moment class differ, so their result informs the calibration and lower-bound comparison rather than being claimed as a theorem-level extension. Donoho (1994) supplies the modulus-of-continuity and affine-recovery blueprint used to turn the weighted boundary geometry into a minimax theorem. Ma and Wang (2020) show how local polynomial correction repairs trimming bias and how weak overlap changes limit laws; the present first proof step is instead a joint interior Riesz-calibration and target empirical process. Orihara, Komukai, and Li (2026) extrapolate a path of overlap-weighted estimands, but their key polynomial approximation condition is not the fixed-Hölder boundary remainder controlled here. Armstrong and Kolesár (2020) supply the fixed-class folded-normal critical value, while Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) explain the extra correction required after inspecting multiple scales. Cai and Low (2004) provide the ordered-modulus language for nonadaptation, and Bull (2012) supplies the multiscale self-similarity mechanism adapted in the open question.
technical_internal_limitation: The critical lower bound cannot follow from one boundary bump: a single bump at \(a=1\) yields only \(n^{-1/2}\). The \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) claim therefore stands or falls with a multiscale mixture whose likelihood divergence remains bounded while separations accumulate across scales. On the upper side, the convex-program stability, maximum-leverage control, spline calibration residual, boundary bias, target empirical noise, conditional multiplier approximation, and studentization must all be proved jointly from the primitive class. The primitive restrictions \(t>1/2\) for density-ratio sieve calibration and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder are maintained separately; neither assumes a fitted-weight rate, optimizer stability, calibration rate, or normal approximation.
honest_scope: The fixed-class statements cover a one-dimensional boundary, known randomized-treatment propensity, bounded outcomes, the standard threshold \(t>1/2\) for the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, the separate product-smoothness relation \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\) for the nuisance-product remainder, fixed transport penalties, and prespecified \((a,s,t,M)\). Each finite-\((n,m)\) minimax class is independent of the asymptotic balance condition; \(m/n\to\kappa\) is imposed only on theorem sequences. Within this covariate-only target model, \(a=0\) reduces to bounded-ratio regular two-sample transport and \(0<a<1\) permits unbounded but square-integrable weights at the same root rate. This reduction is not a specialization of Burman et al.'s target-outcome estimand. No unrestricted adaptive interval is claimed. Joint adaptation to \(a\) and \(s\) is confined to the explicit self-similar class and remains the first-class open-ended question. Multivariate boundary manifolds, observational treatment assignment, and formal sensitivity analysis for transportability are outside this core.
